subject: VectorOps / Redwood: joint cold-tiering cost & architecture proposal
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Levin <sasha@vectorops.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: VectorOps / Redwood: joint cold-tiering cost & architecture proposal

Hi Sasha —

Thanks for the call earlier. Per our discussion, attached is a concise architecture proposal that blends VectorOps' cold-object store tiering with Redwood's hot-index routing. High-level goals: reduce per-query unit cost for long-tail retrievals, avoid unnecessary GPU warmups, and keep SLA impact under 100ms P95 for cached hits.

Key points in the attachment (vec-arch-v1.pdf):
- Hot index: Pinecone-style fast vector lookup for top-k (managed by VectorOps or PGVector for self-hosted customers)
- Cold store: S3-backed dense-blob bucket with metadata indexing (VectorOps handles transparent rehydration)
- Fallback policy: async prefetch + lightweight re-ranking to hide cold latency for user-facing queries
- Cost split proposal: egress and cold egress to be handled by partner for multi-tenant hosted; reserved contract tiering for Dedicated customers

Open questions we flagged on the call for you to review:
1) Encryption-at-rest and KMS flow for rehydration (customer-managed KMS vs shared)
2) Egress accounting and how to meter / invoice for rehydration traffic
3) Expected cold-hit P95 under a 5% cold rate assumption for a 100k qps baseline

Also attaching a simple cost model (cost-model-v1.xlsx) with assumptions. Can you confirm you and your engineering lead are comfortable with the rehydration lifecycle and whether VectorOps can expose a usage endpoint we can poll for billing reconciliation?

If this looks fine, let’s schedule a technical working session next week (30–45m) with your engineering lead and our runtime team (Irene). Vanessa — please advise on commercial guardrails and pricing bands we should present.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Partner Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Sasha Levin <sasha@vectorops.com>

Subject: Re: VectorOps / Redwood: joint cold-tiering cost & architecture proposal

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear brief and the artifacts. Quick answers and a couple of asks from our side: 

On encryption/KMS:
- We support customer-managed KMS for cloud deployments (bring-your-own-key). For our managed offering we can provide a dedicated envelope key per customer — is that acceptable for your SOC2 customers?

On egress metering:
- We can emit an hourly usage feed (S3 manifest + signed URL) or a REST meter endpoint that returns per-customer bytes rehydrated. REST endpoint preferred for reconciliation.

On expected P95 for cold-hit:
- With our baseline rehydration (multi-part GET + small object optimization), in our staging runs we saw 200–400ms P95 for 1–4MB objects from S3 in us-west region. Network variability is the main factor; we can instrument a CDN/edge prefetch to reduce that for hot subsets.

A few clarification requests: 
1) When you say "lightweight re-ranking" — do you expect to do an on-the-fly embedding recompute at the application layer or at the runtime in front of the model?
2) If we expose REST metering, what auth model do you prefer (signed keys vs mutual TLS)?
3) For the Dedicated customers, will Redwood want VectorOps to accept service-level credits if rehydration spikes cause missed throughput?

We’re happy to join the technical session. Our engineering lead, Arjun Patel (arjun@vectorops.com), will be on the call — looping him in when we agree time.

—Sasha
Sasha Levin
Head of Platform Partnerships | VectorOps Inc
+1 (206) 555-0199

Thanks both — good detail from Sasha. A few commercial points to keep us aligned before the tech working session: 

Commercial guardrails (preliminary):
- For Hosted Redwood API customers: we propose a usage surcharge applied when rehydration bytes > 5GB/day per account; suggested starting band $0.02/GB (partner-managed) with a pass-through model on the invoice.
- For Dedicated: include rehydration as part of the reserved capacity contract as an optional add-on (monthly commitment).
- Audit & billing: we need either the REST metering endpoint or hourly S3 manifests for reconciliation — REST endpoint preferred.

Operational asks for the eng session:
- Arjun (VectorOps) to sketch rehydration API (contract + auth) and expected latency percentiles by object size.
- Redwood runtime (Irene) to outline how we surface cache hits/falls through in the Console and whether customers can opt-in to prefetch rules.
- Ben to run a quick sensitivity in the cost-model for egress bands (0.01–0.05 $/GB) so we have numbers to talk about with GTM.

Irene — can you bring a short slide (2 slides) that shows how a 1%, 5%, 10% cold-rate affects P95 and cost per 10k queries? That will help the partner make a case to their customers.

If agreeable, proposed times: Thu 18 Sep 10:00–10:45 PT or Fri 19 Sep 08:00–08:45 PT. Ben — can you confirm availability and we’ll send a meeting invite + agenda.

Vanessa Ortiz
